fullPassage:
Great Opening Lines

You never get a second chance to make a first impression. It is very important to make a good impression on others when we meet them for the first time. But people aren't the only ones who make first impressions — books do as well. A powerful first line of a book can catch readers' attention and make them want to read on. Authors often spend weeks, months, or even years coming up with the perfect opening line for their books. Let's take a look at some of them.

"All children, except one, grow up."
- Peter Pan, J.M. Barrie

No one can stop the sands of time. Every child becomes an adult whether they want to or not. But the opening line of Peter Pan states that there is one child who is the exception to the rule. Peter Pan is a boy who refuses to grow older. He wants to have fun and stay a child forever.

One night in London, Peter Pan and Tinker Bell visit the home of Wendy, John, and Michael. Peter Pan invites them to a fantastic island in the sky called Neverland. It is a magical place where dreams are born and excitement never ends. The children take Peter Pan's hand and their adventure begins. Only children can visit Neverland, and they do not grow up as long as they remain there. They have a wonderful time in Neverland. But in the end, the three children decide to return home and grow up. What is the reason for this unexpected decision? Read the book to find out.

"There is no lake at Camp Green Lake."
- Holes, Louis Sachar

What comes to mind when you hear the word "camp?" Many people would think of fun activities like fishing, having a barbecue, and sleeping under the beautiful stars. So what kind of place do you imagine Camp Green Lake is? Perhaps it is a beautiful place where a green forest surrounds a blue lake. But the first line of Holes paints a different picture. It states that there is no lake there despite its name. Through this irony, Sachar is hinting that Camp Green Lake is not a normal camp with fun and games.

In fact, Camp Green Lake is not a camp at all. Located in the desert, it is like a prison for bad boys. The main character of the book, a teenage boy named Stanley Yelnats, is different from the other boys in the camp. He hasn't done anything wrong. He was just in the wrong place at the wrong time. Stanley and the other boys at Camp Green Lake are expected to improve their character by digging holes every day. Stanley suspects that there is another reason for the digging. Will Stanley successfully dig up the truth about Camp Green Lake?

"It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks were striking thirteen."
- 1984, George Orwell

Typically, clocks strike from one to twelve times. But George Orwell's well-known novel, 1984, opens with the clocks striking thirteen times. In a normal world, a clock striking thirteen is out of the ordinary. But in this mysterious place, it doesn't seem to be unusual. Not just one clock but all clocks strike thirteen here. What's more, the number thirteen is often associated with bad luck in Western cultures. In this way, Orwell hints to the readers that they are about to enter a world that is dark and unfamiliar.

The story takes place in an imaginary country called Oceania in the year 1984. The government tries to control everyone's life. It has even created a new language to limit people's thoughts and expressions. Big Brother, the leader of Oceania, watches everything that goes on through television screens. As long as Big Brother is in power, the people of Oceania will never be free. The main character, Winston Smith, does not agree with what the government is doing. He wants to fight against Big Brother, but he can't do it by himself. Will Winston find others to join him? Or will he give in and be controlled by Big Brother like the rest of the people?

questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 첫인상을 남길 기회는 한 번뿐이다. 책의 첫 문장이 독자의 관심을 사로잡는다. 작가들은 완벽한 첫 문장을 만드는 데 수주~수년을 ③보낸다.
det.analysis: ❌ ③ spends → spend: 주어 'Authors'가 복수이므로 spend. ✅ ① meet: we meet 정상. ✅ ② catch: can catch 정상. ✅ ④ coming: spend time -ing 정상.
det.tip: 주어-동사 수일치: Authors(복수) → spend. Author(단수) → spends

questions.passage: One night in London, Peter Pan and Tinker Bell visit the home of Wendy, John, and Michael. Peter Pan ①<u>invites</u> them to a fantastic island in the sky ②<u>calling</u> Neverland. It is a magical place ③<u>where</u> dreams are born and excitement never ends. The children take Peter Pan's hand and ④<u>their</u> adventure begins.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 피터 팬은 네버랜드라는 환상적인 섬으로 ①초대한다. 네버랜드라고 ②불리는 섬이다. 꿈이 태어나는 ③곳이다. ④그들의 모험이 시작된다.
det.analysis: ❌ ② calling → called: 'an island called Neverland'에서 called는 과거분사(~라 불리는). 섬이 '부르는' 것이 아니라 '불리는' 것이므로 수동. ✅ ① invites: 3인칭 단수 정상. ✅ ③ where: 장소 관계부사 정상. ✅ ④ their: 소유격 정상.
det.tip: called: ~라 불리는 (과거분사/수동), calling: ~를 부르는 (현재분사/능동)

questions.passage: The story takes place in an imaginary country ①<u>called</u> Oceania in the year 1984. The government tries to control everyone's life. It has even created a new language ②<u>to limit</u> people's thoughts and expressions. Big Brother watches everything ③<u>what</u> goes on through television screens. As long as Big Brother is in power, the people of Oceania will never ④<u>be</u> free.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 오세아니아라는 가상 국가에서 벌어진다. 생각을 ②제한하기 위해 새 언어를 만들었다. 빅 브라더는 일어나는 모든 ③것을 지켜본다. 결코 ④자유롭지 못할 것이다.
det.analysis: ❌ ③ what → that: 'everything that goes on' — everything은 선행사이므로 관계대명사 that 사용. what은 선행사를 포함하므로 everything과 중복. ✅ ① called: 과거분사 정상. ✅ ② to limit: 목적 to부정사 정상. ✅ ④ be: will never be 정상.
det.tip: everything/anything/nothing + that (관계대명사). what = the thing that (선행사 포함이라 everything과 함께 불가)

questions.passage: No one can stop the sands of time. Every child becomes an adult whether they want to or not. But the opening line of Peter Pan states that there is one child who is the ①<u>exception</u> to the rule. Peter Pan is a boy who refuses to grow ②<u>younger</u>. He wants to have fun and stay a child ③<u>forever</u>. One night in London, Peter Pan and Tinker Bell ④<u>visit</u> the home of Wendy.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 세월의 흐름을 멈출 수 없다. 그 법칙의 ①예외인 아이가 있다. 피터 팬은 나이 ②어려지는(→들어가는) 것을 거부한다. ③영원히 아이로 남고 싶다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② younger(더 어린): 원문은 older(더 나이든). 나이가 '드는 것'을 거부하는 맥락. younger는 반대. ❌ ①③④ 원문 그대로.
det.tip: grow older: 나이가 들다 (↔ grow younger: 더 어려지다)

questions.passage: The government tries to control everyone's life. It has even created a new language to limit people's thoughts and expressions. Big Brother, the leader of Oceania, watches everything that goes on through television screens. As long as Big Brother is in power, the people of Oceania will never be free. The main character, Winston Smith, does not ①<u>agree</u> with what the government is doing. He wants to fight ②<u>against</u> Big Brother, but he can't do it by ③<u>himself</u>. Or will he ④<u>resist</u> and be controlled by Big Brother like the rest of the people?
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 정부가 하는 일에 ①동의하지 않는다. 빅 브라더에 ②맞서 싸우고 싶다. ③혼자서는 할 수 없다. ④저항하고(→굴복하고) 통제받을까?
det.analysis: ❌ ④ resist(저항하다): 원문은 give in(굴복하다). 'be controlled by Big Brother'와 연결되므로 '굴복'이 맥락에 적절. resist는 fight against와 같은 의미로 Or 이후 대비가 안 됨. ✅ ①②③ 원문 그대로.
det.tip: give in(굴복하다) ↔ resist(저항하다), fight against(맞서 싸우다)

questions.passage: You never get a second chance to make a first impression. It is very important to make a good impression on others when we meet them for the first time. But people aren't the only ones who make first impressions — books do as well. A powerful first line of a book can __________ and make them want to read on.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 책의 강렬한 첫 문장은 독자들의 관심을 사로잡고 계속 읽고 싶게 만든다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② catch readers' attention: '독자의 관심을 사로잡다'. want to read on으로 이어지는 맥락. ❌ ① confuse(혼란): 부적절. ❌ ③ change habits(습관 변경): 무관. ❌ ④ limit choices(선택 제한): 무관.
det.tip: catch one's attention: ~의 관심을 사로잡다, read on: 계속 읽다

questions.passage: What comes to mind when you hear the word "camp?" Many people would think of fun activities like fishing, having a barbecue, and sleeping under the beautiful stars. det.korean: 이름에 '호수'가 있지만 호수가 없다. 이런 역설을 통해 평범한 캠프가 아니라고 암시한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④ irony: 이름(Green Lake)과 실제(호수 없음)의 모순 = '역설'. ❌ ① humor(유머): 재미있는 상황 아님. ❌ ② tragedy(비극): 부적절. ❌ ③ mystery(미스터리): 역설과 다름.
det.tip: irony: 역설, 아이러니 (= 기대와 현실의 모순)

questions.passage: No one can stop the sands of time. Every child becomes an adult whether they want to or not. But the opening line of Peter Pan states that there is one child who is the exception to the rule. Peter Pan is a boy who refuses to grow older. He wants to have fun and stay a child forever.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 피터 팬은 빨리 어른이 되고 싶어 한다.
모든 어린이는 예외 없이 어른이 된다.
세월의 흐름을 멈출 수 있는 방법이 있다.
피터 팬은 영원히 아이로 남고 싶어 한다.

det.korean: 피터 팬은 나이 드는 것을 거부하고 영원히 아이로 남고 싶어 한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④ 'wants to stay a child forever' 직접 확인. ❌ ① refuses to grow older(반대). ❌ ② 예외가 있음(exception). ❌ ③ 멈출 수 없음(no one can stop).
det.tip: stay a child forever: 영원히 아이로 남다

questions.passage: In fact, Camp Green Lake is not a camp at all. Located in the desert, it is like a prison for bad boys. The main character of the book, a teenage boy named Stanley Yelnats, is different from the other boys in the camp. He hasn't done anything wrong.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 초록 호수 캠프는 사막에 위치해 있다.
초록 호수 캠프는 호수가 있는 아름다운 곳이다.
스탠리는 나쁜 행동을 해서 캠프에 왔다.
캠프의 모든 소년들은 스탠리와 같은 처지이다.

det.korean: 사막에 위치한 감옥 같은 곳이다. 스탠리는 잘못한 것이 없고 다른 소년들과 다르다.
det.analysis: ✅ ① 'Located in the desert' 직접 확인. ❌ ② 호수 없음. ❌ ③ 잘못 안 했음. ❌ ④ 다른 소년들과 다름.
det.tip: located in: ~에 위치한

questions.passage: The government tries to control everyone's life. It has even created a new language to limit people's thoughts and expressions. Big Brother, the leader of Oceania, watches everything that goes on through television screens. As long as Big Brother is in power, the people of Oceania will never be free. The main character, Winston Smith, does not agree with what the government is doing.

ch: 빅 브라더가 집권하는 한 자유는 없다.

det.korean: 정부는 새 언어를 만들었다. 빅 브라더는 TV로 감시한다. 윈스턴은 정부에 동의하지 않는다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③ 불일치: 'does not agree with what the government is doing'. 동의하지 않음. ❌ ①②④ 일치.
det.tip: does not agree with: ~에 동의하지 않다

questions.passage: You never get a second chance to make a first impression. But people aren't the only ones who make first impressions — books do as well. A powerful first line of a book can catch readers' attention and make them want to read on. Authors often spend weeks, months, or even years coming up with the perfect opening line for their books.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 독자를 사로잡는 소설 첫 문장의 중요성

det.korean: 사람뿐 아니라 책도 첫인상을 남긴다. 강렬한 첫 문장이 독자의 관심을 사로잡는다. 작가들은 완벽한 첫 문장에 오랜 시간을 투자한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② 첫 문장의 힘과 중요성이 핵심. ❌ ①③④ 부분적이거나 무관.
det.tip: opening line: 첫 문장

questions.passage: Typically, clocks strike from one to twelve times. But George Orwell's well-known novel, 1984, opens with the clocks striking thirteen times. In a normal world, a clock striking thirteen is out of the ordinary. What's more, the number thirteen is often associated with bad luck in Western cultures. In this way, Orwell hints to the readers that they are about to enter a world that is dark and unfamiliar.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 오웰이 첫 문장을 통해 전달하려는 메시지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 13번 치는 시계, 불운과 연관된 숫자. 곧 어둡고 생소한 세계에 들어갈 것이라는 암시.
det.analysis: ✅ ① 'dark and unfamiliar' 세계에 들어갈 것이라는 암시. ❌ ② 시간 평등 아님. ❌ ③ bad luck(불운). ❌ ④ 시계 정확성 아님.
det.tip: hint to the readers: 독자에게 암시하다

questions.passage: What comes to mind when you hear the word "camp?" Many people would think of fun activities like fishing, having a barbecue, and sleeping under the beautiful stars. But the first line of Holes <u>paints a different picture</u>. It states that there is no lake there despite its name.

det.tip: catch one's attention: 관심을 사로잡다, make + O + V: ~가 …하게 만들다

questions.ans: A powerful first line of a book can catch readers' attention and make them want to read on

questions.passage:
Only children can visit Neverland, and they do not grow up as long as they remain there. They have a wonderful time in Neverland. But in the end, the three children decide to return home and grow up. What is the reason for this unexpected decision? Read the book to find out. "There is no lake at Camp Green Lake."
- Holes, Louis Sachar

What comes to mind when you hear the word "camp?" Many people would think of fun activities like fishing, having a barbecue, and sleeping under the beautiful stars. So what kind of place do you imagine Camp Green Lake is? Perhaps it is a beautiful place where a green forest surrounds a blue lake.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 세 아이가 최종적으로 내린 결정을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

"세 아이는 집으로 돌아가서 __________ 결심한다."

※ 영어 2단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 세 아이는 집으로 돌아가서 성장하기로 결심한다.
det.analysis: 'decide to return home and grow up'에서 grow up이 핵심.
det.tip: grow up: 성장하다, 어른이 되다

questions.passage: The government tries to control everyone's life. It has even created a new language to limit people's thoughts and expressions. Big Brother, the leader of Oceania, watches everything that goes on through television screens. As long as Big Brother is in power, the people of Oceania will never be free. The main character, Winston Smith, does not agree with what the government is doing. He wants to fight against Big Brother, but he can't do it by himself. Will Winston find others to join him? Or will he give in and be controlled by Big Brother like the rest of the people?
questions.stem:
위 글에서 윈스턴이 빅 브라더에 대해 하고 싶은 행동을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

"윈스턴은 빅 브라더에 맞서 __________ 싶어 한다."

※ 영어 1단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 윈스턴은 빅 브라더에 맞서 싸우고 싶어 한다.
det.analysis: 'wants to fight against Big Brother'에서 fight가 핵심.
det.tip: fight against: ~에 맞서 싸우다
